incident: BlackSuit ransomware via Cobalt Strike beachhead (DFIR Report, intrusion Dec 2023, published 2024-08-26)

sources.title: BlackSuit Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2024-08-26)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (Cobalt Strike beacon on beachhead, delivery unknown), hops (SMB/ADMIN$ beacons, RDP from DC X to file/backup servers, C$ ransomware push), credential access (AS-REP/Kerberoast, LSASS), TTR 328h / 15 days, impact

narrative_before: In December 2023 an intrusion began with the execution of an unusually large Cobalt Strike beacon (RtWin64.exe) on a beachhead host; the delivery method could not be determined (DFIR Report). About six hours later the actor ran systeminfo/nltest, performed AS-REP roasting and Kerberoasting against two domain controllers with Rubeus in memory, and ran SharpHound. Ten minutes later they moved a beacon over SMB to a second workstation via a service and accessed LSASS there; on day two beacons were spread to workstations and servers and RDP was used, with SystemBC proxies dropped on a file server. A domain controller (DC X) became the main pivot; RDP from it reached a file server and a backup server for discovery. After pauses (days 3-6, 8-10, then five days), on day 15 the actor ran ADFind and Get-DataInfo.ps1, pushed qwe.exe (BlackSuit) over the C$ share and executed it via RDP sessions from DC X; vssadmin deleted shadow copies before encryption. Time to ransomware was just under 328 hours over 15 calendar days (DFIR Report).

detection_moments.description: Earliest sign: execution of an unusually large Cobalt Strike beacon on the beachhead host; no follow-up for ~6 hours.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the initial sign being the execution of an unusually large-sized Cobalt Strike beacon. After the beacon's execution, there was no immediate follow-up activity' - BlackSuit Ransomware, DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: End of day 2, after which the intrusion went silent: Kerberoasting/AS-REP from beachhead, LSASS on second workstation, beacons on DCs, workstations and servers, SystemBC C2 on file server, RDP discovery on backup server.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Throughout the second day of the intrusion, the threat actor deployed multiple Cobalt Strike beacons on workstations and servers and also used RDP for further lateral movement... After a busy second day of activity, the intrusion went silent.' - BlackSuit Ransomware, DFIR Report

attack_path: Cobalt Strike beacon copied over SMB and executed via service (psexec); LSASS access on target - T1021.002 / T1569.002 / T1003.001
AS-REP roasting + Kerberoasting with Rubeus against DCs, SMB beacons distributed to DC - T1558.003 / T1558.004 / T1021.002
RDP from DC X, registry change to enable RDP, SystemBC SC.exe/socks32.exe executed manually - T1021.001 / T1112 / T1090
RDP from DC for discovery - T1021.001
qwe.exe (BlackSuit) copied via C$ share and executed via RDP; vssadmin shadow deletion - T1021.002 / T1021.001 / T1486 / T1490
ambiguities: Initial access delivery method unknown per report ('could not be determined'); no technique ID assigned to entry.
Report does not say when/if the victim detected the intrusion; m1 is the report's 'earliest sign', m2 is the end of the first active phase.
Counts of 'workstations and servers' that received beacons on day 2 are not given; represented as pc_3, pc_4, srv_1 (3 generic machines).
Which host distributed the beacon to DC Y is not stated; link pc_beachhead->dc_y assumed from 'SMB beacons... distributed on the beachhead and on a domain controller'.
Number of DCs: report names DC X, DC Y and 'the second domain controller'; modelled as two.
Scope of encryption ('key endpoints', 'various systems') not quantified.
